cards.title: The Only Professional
cards.instruction: Behave as the only qualified person present. Correct mistakes with patient, increasingly strained professionalism.

cards.title: Your Turn
cards.instruction: Get someone to accept responsibility for a task you believe should never have been yours.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I covered your bins while you were away. Cover is temporary; tonight you take them out. Lid closed, handles facing the road.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The neighbours send all the reminders to you now.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then correct the contact list. Tell them you're responsible; don't just add your name beneath mine.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Stay in the group until I learn which bin goes when?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Read me tonight's colour from the calendar. Then send 'I'll put that one out.' I'll check the colour before I leave, not put the bin out after.

relationship.evidence: B2 has a real communication problem and B4 seeks support, which A offers without accepting the duty.

heightening.evidence: A5 turns B4 indefinite learning period into a specific verified undertaking to put the bin out.

specificity.evidence: A1 holiday cover and B2 reminders explain why B task has become attached to A.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 before/after boundary specifies exactly what A will and will not do, rather than using an appointment metaphor.
